- Overestimate prices when sentiment is positive or neutral (especially after recent spikes), especially in early forecast windows.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is negative or shows strong downward momentum, particularly in mid-to-late forecast windows.
- Overshoot after sharp upward sentiment spikes; reduce forecast peak by 5–10% in subsequent periods.
- Mean-revert forecasts when sentiment shows divergence from historical mean (e.g., sentiment >0.7 with price rising, then sentiment drops below 0.3).
- Lagged price corrections: if sentiment turns negative after a forecast peak, reduce forecast by 3–5% per day until sentiment stabilizes.
- Avoid overconfidence in short-term forecasts when sentiment is volatile; use 3–5 day smoothing for sentiment-weighted adjustments.
- For 30-day forecasts, reduce forecast by 1–2% if sentiment is below 0.3 for 3+ consecutive days.
- If sentiment is consistently above 0.7 and price is rising, cap forecast at 10% above recent 7-day average to avoid over-optimism.
